# Piedmont Triad Equity Solutions

Piedmont Triad Equity Solutions is a nationwide surplus fund recovery firm based in North Carolina that helps former property owners identify and reclaim funds left over after foreclosures, tax sales, and public auctions. The brand positions itself around trust, transparency, and zero financial risk to the client — operating on a contingency basis where they only get paid upon successful recovery. The firm emphasizes confidentiality, a step-by-step guided process, and a dedicated recovery specialist for every claim, projecting a professional yet approachable tone aimed at individuals who may be unaware they are owed money.

Understanding Your Rights


## What Are Surplus Funds?



Surplus funds may arise when a property is sold through foreclosure, tax sale, or a similar public auction process, and the final sale price exceeds the total amount owed on the property. As part of our financial recovery services, we help former owners identify and reclaim these funds.









When a property is sold through a tax sale, foreclosure, or similar public process, the remaining balance — after all liens, taxes, fees, and other obligations are satisfied — is generally referred to as surplus funds or overage funds. These amounts are held through county-specific procedures and may be available for review by former owners or related parties.


The availability, amount, and eligibility for surplus funds are determined through public records and county-specific legal requirements. Many former property owners are unaware these funds exist or that they may have a valid claim. Our role is to identify, review, and guide eligible claimants through every step of the recovery process — at no upfront cost.















Example Scenario


### Surplus Funds Calculation





If a property has $15,000 owed in back taxes and is sold for $300,000:



Sale Price
$300,000


Amount Owed (taxes, liens, fees & obligations)
− $15,000



Surplus Funds
$285,000




The above is a simplified illustrative example. Actual surplus fund amounts, eligibility, and procedures are determined by public records and applicable county and state regulations.















Public-Record Review


We analyze publicly available county records to identify potential surplus funds associated with your property.












County-Specific Procedures


Every county has distinct legal requirements. Our team navigates jurisdiction-specific processes on your behalf.












No Upfront Fees


We operate exclusively on a contingency basis — you pay nothing unless we successfully recover funds on your behalf.












Confidential Review


All claim reviews are handled with complete discretion. Your personal and financial information remains strictly confidential.


























Our Financial Recovery Services


## How the Recovery Process Works







A clear, guided path from discovery to disbursement — at no upfront cost to you.














01





### Research & Identification


We conduct a thorough review of publicly available county records, auction outcomes, and foreclosure filings to identify surplus funds associated with your former property. If a recoverable balance is located, we contact you directly.








02





### Claim Preparation & Filing


Your dedicated recovery specialist prepares all required documentation and executes the formal claim on your behalf. We handle every form, affidavit, and supporting record required by the applicable county or state authority.








03





### Agency & Court Coordination


We liaise directly with the relevant government agencies, county clerks, and court offices to advance your claim through the legal process. Our team monitors status, responds to requests, and ensures nothing falls through the cracks.








04





### Funds Disbursement


Once approved, surplus funds are released and disbursed to you per the terms of your signed recovery agreement. Our fee is collected only upon successful recovery — you pay nothing unless we deliver results.

Got Questions?

## Frequently AskedQuestions


We believe in full transparency. Here are the answers to the questions we hear most from homeowners across the Piedmont Triad.








What is unclaimed equity and how do I know if I have any?






Unclaimed equity refers to money that is legally owed to you from a property sale — often after a foreclosure or tax deed sale — that was never collected. When a property sells for more than what was owed, the surplus funds belong to the former owner. Many homeowners don't even know this money exists. We review public records to identify if you have a claim and guide you through every step of recovering it.






How much does it cost to work with Piedmont Triad Equity Solutions?






There are  no upfront costs  to you. We work on a contingency basis, meaning we only get paid when you successfully recover your funds. Our fee is a percentage of the recovered amount, agreed upon before we begin — so you never pay out of pocket and there are no hidden charges.






How long does the recovery process take?






Timelines vary depending on the complexity of your case and the county where the property was located. Most straightforward claims are resolved within  60 to 120 days . We keep you informed at every stage and work diligently to move your case forward as quickly as possible.






Is this service available if my property was foreclosed years ago?






Possibly, yes. Surplus funds can often be claimed for several years after a foreclosure or tax sale, but there are strict deadlines that vary by state and county. The sooner you reach out, the better your chances. We'll review your situation at no cost and let you know right away whether a valid claim still exists.






Do I need a lawyer to reclaim my equity?






In some cases, an attorney may be required to file a petition with the court. When that's needed, we work with a trusted network of licensed attorneys who specialize in surplus fund recovery. We coordinate everything on your behalf so you don't have to navigate the legal system alone.






How do I get started?






Getting started is simple and completely free. Just reach out to us by phone or through our contact form. We'll conduct a free, no-obligation review of your situation, confirm whether funds are available, and walk you through the next steps — all at zero cost to you until your money is recovered.










Still have questions? We're here to help — reach out any time.


Talk to Us Today

# Your Dedicated Recovery Process, Step by Step





At Piedmont Triad Equity Solutions, we specialize in identifying publicly available records to determine whether surplus funds may be owed to you following a foreclosure, tax sale, or public auction — and we guide you through every step of the recovery process at no upfront cost.









## How Our Financial Recovery Services Work


When a property is sold through foreclosure, tax sale, or a similar public process, the final sale price may exceed the total amount owed. The remaining balance — after all liens, taxes, fees, and obligations are satisfied — is known as surplus or overage funds. These funds are held through county procedures and may be available to former owners or related parties.


Our team reviews publicly available records to identify whether surplus funds are associated with a property you previously owned. Once identified, your dedicated recovery specialist will walk you through the claims process from start to finish, handling the complexity so you don't have to.

Common Questions



## Frequently Asked Questions



We understand that surplus fund recovery is an unfamiliar process for most people. Below are the most common questions our clients ask before starting their claim — answered plainly, without legal jargon.








01


### What are surplus funds?


Surplus funds — sometimes called overage funds — are the remaining balance left over after a property is sold through a foreclosure, tax sale, or public auction and the total amount owed (taxes, liens, fees, and obligations) is satisfied. If a property sells for more than what was owed, the difference may be held through county procedures and could be available to the former owner.






02


### Who may qualify to receive surplus funds?


Former property owners, heirs, and certain related parties may be eligible to claim surplus funds associated with a property that was sold through a foreclosure or tax sale. Eligibility is determined by public records and county-specific procedures. Our team reviews available records to assess whether a claim may be viable for your specific situation.






03


### How does the recovery process work?


We begin with a confidential records review to identify whether surplus funds may be associated with your property. If a potential claim is found, your dedicated recovery specialist guides you through each step — from document preparation and filing to coordinating with the appropriate county office — until the funds are successfully recovered on your behalf.






04


### How long does the process typically take?


Timelines vary depending on the county, the complexity of the claim, and the responsiveness of the relevant agencies. Most claims are resolved within 60 to 180 days from the point of engagement. Your recovery specialist will provide a realistic timeline estimate once your case is reviewed and we have a clearer picture of the jurisdiction involved.






05


### Are there any upfront costs or fees?


No. Piedmont Triad Equity Solutions operates entirely on a contingency basis — meaning we are only compensated if and when your claim is successfully recovered. There are no upfront fees, no out-of-pocket expenses, and no hidden charges at any stage of the process. Our financial recovery services carry zero financial risk to you.






06


### Is the government holding my funds — can I claim them myself?


In many cases, surplus funds are held by a county clerk, court registry, or similar government office. While it is technically possible to file a claim independently, the process involves specific legal filings, documentation requirements, and deadlines that vary by jurisdiction. Many former owners are unaware these funds exist at all. We handle the entire process so you don't have to navigate it alone.






07


### How is my personal information protected?


Confidentiality is a core commitment at every stage of our engagement. Your personal details, property information, and claim status are handled with strict discretion and are never shared with third parties beyond what is required to process your claim. We take the privacy of every client seriously, regardless of claim size or complexity.






08


### Can you guarantee that funds will be recovered?


We cannot guarantee a specific outcome, as every claim is subject to public records, county procedures, and applicable legal requirements beyond our control. What we can guarantee is a thorough, professional review of your case and dedicated representation throughout the process. If we do not believe a viable claim exists, we will tell you clearly before proceeding.






09


### Am I obligated to proceed after submitting my information?


Absolutely not. Submitting your information for an initial review carries no obligation to proceed. Our preliminary review is provided at no cost and with no commitment required on your part. You are free to decide whether to move forward after receiving our findings — there is no pressure at any stage of the process.






10


### What happens after I submit my claim information?


Once you submit your details, a dedicated recovery specialist will be assigned to your case within one to two business days. They will conduct a confidential review of publicly available records, confirm whether a potential claim exists, and reach out to walk you through the next steps. You will have a single point of contact throughout the entire process.










Still have questions? Your dedicated specialist is ready to help.

Important Notice



## Understanding What Client Experiences Tell You





The client experiences shared on this page reflect individual outcomes from specific surplus fund recovery matters. Each case presented a unique set of circumstances, and the results achieved were shaped by the particular facts of that property, county, and legal process.


Surplus fund recovery is not a guaranteed service. The availability of funds, the amount recoverable, and the timeline for resolution vary considerably from case to case. Piedmont Triad Equity Solutions provides professional financial recovery services on a contingency basis — we only receive compensation upon a successful recovery — but we make no representation that any particular outcome will be achieved in your matter.


Past results in surplus fund recovery proceedings are not indicative of future outcomes. You should not rely on any client experience described on this site as a prediction, promise, or guarantee of what may occur in your individual case.



Piedmont Triad Equity Solutions operates with full transparency as part of our commitment to ethical financial recovery services.













### Result Variability Notice


Factors that affect every claim






- 01 #### Property History & Record Completeness Each property carries a distinct ownership and lien history. Incomplete or disputed records can affect the identification of eligible claimants and the amount of surplus funds available for recovery.

- 02 #### County Procedures & Jurisdictional Rules Surplus fund procedures differ by county and state. The specific rules governing how funds are held, claimed, and distributed are determined by local statutes and the practices of individual county offices.

- 03 #### Court Timelines & Scheduling Court dockets, hearing schedules, and judicial review periods vary by jurisdiction. These timelines are outside our control and can affect the overall duration of the recovery process in any given case.

- 04 #### Administrative & Competing Claim Factors Competing lienholders, creditor claims, or administrative holds placed by a government entity may reduce the net amount recoverable. Final disbursements are subject to satisfaction of all valid prior obligations.







This notice applies to all client experiences, case summaries, and recovery amounts referenced throughout this website. For questions about your specific situation, contact a dedicated recovery specialist.

About Our Firm



# Piedmont TriadEquity Solutions







Piedmont Triad Equity Solutions is a nationwide surplus fund recovery firm headquartered in North Carolina. We specialize in helping former property owners identify and reclaim funds left over after foreclosures, tax sales, and public auctions — money that is rightfully theirs, yet often goes unclaimed.


Our practice is built on a foundation of trust, transparency, and confidentiality. We operate entirely on a contingency basis, meaning there are never any upfront fees — our financial recovery services are compensated only upon a successful recovery. Every client receives a dedicated recovery specialist who guides them through each step of the process, ensuring clarity and peace of mind from first contact to final resolution.

Piedmont Triad Equity Solutions



## Our Charter of Service










The following guarantees form the foundation of every engagement we undertake. These are not aspirations — they are binding commitments that govern our financial recovery services from the first consultation to successful fund recovery.




- I ### No Upfront Fees — Ever We operate exclusively on a contingency basis. You pay nothing unless we successfully recover funds on your behalf. There are no retainers, no application fees, and no hidden charges at any stage of the process. Our success is directly tied to yours.

- II ### Complete Transparency at Every Stage You will receive clear, timely updates throughout your claim. We explain every step, every document, and every timeline in plain language — no legal jargon, no ambiguity. Our financial recovery process is designed to keep you fully informed and in control at all times.

- III ### Strict Confidentiality of Your Information All personal details, property records, and claim-related information you share with us are handled with the highest standard of discretion. We never share, sell, or disclose your information to third parties outside the direct requirements of your recovery claim.

- IV ### A Dedicated Recovery Specialist for Every Claim Every client is assigned a single, named recovery specialist who manages your case from intake through resolution. You will always know who to contact, and your specialist will know the full history of your claim — no handoffs, no confusion, no starting over.



























What We Do


## Our Capabilities in Surplus Fund Recovery





We provide structured, professional financial recovery services focused on public record research, coordinated claim support, and transparent client guidance — with no upfront cost and no obligation to proceed. We do not provide legal, tax, or financial advice.













### Public Record Research



We conduct thorough reviews of county records, tax sale filings, foreclosure proceedings, and public auction documents to identify whether surplus funds may be associated with a former property. Our research draws exclusively from publicly available sources to determine potential fund availability and eligibility status.


- County tax sale & foreclosure records

- Public auction surplus identification

- Lien, fee & obligation verification












### Claim Coordination Support

### No Guarantees of Recovery




The information provided on this website does not constitute a guarantee, promise, or representation that surplus funds exist, are recoverable, or will be recovered in any specific amount or timeframe. Every claim is unique. The existence and availability of surplus funds depend on a wide range of factors, including but not limited to the specific county, jurisdiction, applicable state statutes, outstanding liens, legal challenges, and the timing of any claim submission.


Past results achieved for other clients are not indicative of future outcomes. Piedmont Triad Equity Solutions makes no warranties, express or implied, regarding the likelihood or amount of any recovery.









02

### Outcomes Vary by Circumstances




Recovery outcomes vary significantly depending on individual circumstances. Factors such as the type of sale (tax sale, foreclosure, public auction), the jurisdiction in which the property was located, the length of time since the sale, the presence of competing claimants, and applicable state or local laws all influence whether surplus funds may be available and whether a claim can be successfully processed.


No two cases are identical. The evaluation of your potential claim is conducted on an individual basis and reflects only the publicly available information at the time of review.









03

### Informational and Evaluation Purposes Only

# Check If You May Be Eligiblefor Surplus Funds





By submitting an inquiry here, you are beginning a free review of publicly available records — you are not committing to representation or any financial obligation. Our financial recovery services team will assess whether surplus funds may be associated with a property in your name, at no cost and with no pressure to proceed.

### Confidential Review

### No Obligation to Proceed

Eligibility Overview



## Do You Qualify for Surplus Fund Recovery?


Review the situations and qualifications below to understand whether you or someone you know may be entitled to unclaimed surplus funds from a property sale event.

















### Likely Situations


Your property may have generated surplus funds if any of the following apply





- Mortgage Foreclosure Your lender initiated foreclosure proceedings and the property was sold at auction

- Tax Sale or Tax Deed Sale The county or municipality sold the property due to unpaid property taxes

- Public Auction Sale The property was sold through a government-administered or court-supervised public auction

- Sheriff's Sale A court judgment led to the sheriff's office conducting a forced sale of the property

- Court-Ordered Sale A judge ordered the property sold as part of a legal proceeding or dispute resolution

- Probate or Estate Sale A property belonging to a deceased owner was sold through probate or estate administration

- Unsure of Your Situation? If you are uncertain whether a qualifying sale event occurred, our team can review publicly available records on your behalf at no cost












### Who May Qualify


Surplus funds may be available to individuals or parties directly connected to the original property







Primary Claimants





Former Property Owners

Individuals who held title to the property at the time of the qualifying sale event and did not receive the full remaining balance after all obligations were satisfied







Estate & Inheritance





Heirs of Deceased Owners

Family members, beneficiaries, or legal heirs of a former property owner who passed away before or after the qualifying sale event, where the estate may retain a rightful interest in unclaimed funds







Investment & Commercial





Real Estate Investors & Entities

Investors, LLCs, or corporate entities that held ownership interest in a property that was subsequently sold through a qualifying public or court-supervised sale process











Eligibility is determined on a case-by-case basis through public record review. There is no cost to find out whether funds may be available — our financial recovery services operate entirely on a contingency basis.

What Happens Next


## Your Submission Is in Good Hands







Once we receive your information, our team follows a careful, structured review process. Here is exactly what our financial recovery services team does on your behalf — at no cost or obligation to you.









01



### Review Public Property Records


We examine publicly available property records, county auction data, and tax sale documentation associated with the address and ownership information you provided. This research is conducted entirely using official public sources.








02



### Check for Surplus Fund Matches


Our specialists cross-reference your submission against known surplus fund records and overage accounts. We look for any remaining balance that may have been generated when the final sale price exceeded the total amount owed on the property.








03



### We Inform You of Next Steps


If a potential match is identified, a dedicated recovery specialist will contact you directly to explain the findings, outline the path forward, and answer any questions — with no pressure and no upfront fees required at any stage.








04



### No Match? No Further Action Needed


If our review does not identify a surplus fund match for your property, we will let you know and no further action is required on your part. There is nothing to pay and no obligation — your submission carries zero financial risk.

# Accessibility Statement

## 1. Accessibility Policy

- Screen reader compatibility

- Appropriate color contrast

- Flexible and scalable font sizes

- Descriptive image alt text

- Hierarchical heading structure

- Clear and descriptive links

- Support for 200% zoom without content loss

The website complies with WCAG 2.1 Level AA, which includes:


- Perceivable: Information is presented in ways users can perceive

- Operable: Interface components are operable

- Understandable: Information and user interface are understandable

- Robust: Content can be interpreted by a variety of technologies

- JAWS (Windows)

- VoiceOver (Mac/iOS)

- TalkBack (Android)

- Dragon NaturallySpeaking

- Switch navigation

- Automated accessibility testing tools

- Manual testing with screen readers

- Keyboard-only navigation

- Color contrast verification

- Testing with users with disabilities
